misconceptions.name: Forgets to carry
misconceptions.description: Writes each column sum mod 10 and never carries: 47 + 38 written as 75.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Place-value chart; exchange 10 ones for a ten with rods before recording

misconceptions.name: Carry placed one column too far left
misconceptions.description: The carry is added two columns left instead of one: 47 + 38 written as 175.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Column chart with the carry written above the correct column; two worked examples

misconceptions.name: Writes the whole column sum instead of regrouping
misconceptions.description: Writes the full column sums side by side: 47 + 38 written as 715.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ten-frame / rods: 'only one digit fits in a column'

misconceptions.name: Drops the final carry-out (76+54 -> 30)
misconceptions.description: Drops the carry out of the last column: 76 + 54 written as 30.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Estimate first; 'can the answer be smaller than the bigger number?'

misconceptions.name: Fact off by one
misconceptions.description: The answer is one more than the correct total: 47 + 38 written as 86.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Number bonds; ten-frame fluency

misconceptions.name: Tens miscounted
misconceptions.description: The answer is ten more than the correct total: 47 + 38 written as 95.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Count in tens on a 100-square

misconceptions.name: Subtracted instead of adding
misconceptions.description: Writes the difference where the sum was asked: 47 + 38 written as 9.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the question aloud; identify the operation word

misconceptions.name: Subtracts the smaller digit from the larger regardless of row ('neeche wala number')
misconceptions.description: Takes the smaller digit from the larger in every column, whichever row it sits in: 62 - 27 written as 45.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Rods: show that the top number is the whole; act out the exchange

misconceptions.name: Exchanges but does not reduce the lender column
misconceptions.description: Adds ten to the column but leaves the lender column unchanged: 62 - 27 written as 45.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Cross out and rewrite the lender digit before subtracting

misconceptions.name: Across zero: zero lends but the column to its left is not reduced
misconceptions.description: The zero becomes 9 and lends, but the column left of it keeps its value: 302 - 178 written as 224.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Three-column rods; exchange a hundred for ten tens first

misconceptions.name: Across zero: zero becomes 10 and stays 10 (should be 9)
misconceptions.description: Takes from the left column correctly but leaves the zero as 10: 302 - 178 written as 134.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Number line count-up as a check

misconceptions.name: Fact off by one
misconceptions.description: The answer is one less than the correct difference: 62 - 27 written as 34.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Number bonds; count-up on a number line

misconceptions.name: Tens miscounted
misconceptions.description: The answer is ten more than the correct difference: 62 - 27 written as 45.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Count back in tens on a 100-square

misconceptions.name: Added instead of subtracting
misconceptions.description: Writes the sum where the difference was asked: 62 - 27 written as 89.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the question aloud; identify the operation word

misconceptions.name: Subtraction means make smaller
misconceptions.description: Fails compare and missing-part situations, where the answer is found by counting up.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Probe with 5 total, 2 red, unknown blue.

misconceptions.name: Digits are independent
misconceptions.description: Treats 43 as a 4 and a 3 with no relation between them.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask what the 4 represents in 43.

misconceptions.name: Regrouping changes the total
misconceptions.description: Thinks 42 becomes 3 + 12, or some other altered total, once it is regrouped.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Represent both decompositions with blocks.

misconceptions.name: Exchange is a rule without meaning
misconceptions.description: Can execute the rote steps of an exchange but cannot say what was traded or why the total is unchanged.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask what was traded and why the value stayed the same.

misconceptions.name: Column misalignment
misconceptions.description: Places ones under tens when writing the numbers into columns.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Visual place-value columns with snap-to-grid.

misconceptions.name: Compensation sign error
misconceptions.description: Adjusts in the wrong direction, doing 52 - 29 as 52 - 30 - 1.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Use an algebraic balance visualisation.

misconceptions.name: Counts inefficiently
misconceptions.description: Can solve, but with excessive one-by-one counting marks.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask the learner to create the largest sensible jumps.

misconceptions.name: Pattern overgeneralisation
misconceptions.description: Chooses subtraction because a keyword such as 'left' appears in the question.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Give a non-subtraction context containing the keyword.

misconceptions.name: Horizontal-to-vertical conversion shifts the shorter number left
misconceptions.description: Rewrites 342 + 5 into columns with the 5 under the tens or the hundreds; the arithmetic that follows is correct for what was written down.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Rewrite three horizontal questions into a printed place-value grid before calculating anything.
misconceptions.source: SPEC.md section 3.4 (taxonomy section 11 error list); visible only in the working box

misconceptions.name: Aligns unequal-length operands from the left, not the ones
misconceptions.description: Lines the two numbers up at their leftmost digit, so 342 + 5 is computed as 342 + 500.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read both numbers into a place-value chart ones-first, then check the ones column before starting.
misconceptions.source: SPEC.md section 3.4 (taxonomy section 11 error list); computable from the operands, but the predictor is not yet in assess/misconceptions.py

misconceptions.name: Assumes a carry is always 1
misconceptions.description: Carries 1 when the column total is 20 or more, so 9 + 8 + 7 in the ones column carries 1 instead of 2.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Three-addend columns with rods: count how many complete tens the column made before writing the carry.
misconceptions.source: SPEC.md section 3.4 (taxonomy section 11 error list); computable from the operands, but the predictor is not yet in assess/misconceptions.py

misconceptions.name: Drops a leading, trailing or internal zero when writing the answer
misconceptions.description: Records 495 + 505 as 100 rather than 1000, or 705 - 201 as 54 rather than 504.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Write the answer into a place-value grid and say the value of every column, including the empty ones.
misconceptions.source: SPEC.md section 3.4 (taxonomy section 11 error list); computable from the operands, but the predictor is not yet in assess/misconceptions.py

misconceptions.name: Finds a missing digit that works in its own column but not across the carry
misconceptions.description: Solves the column in isolation and ignores what the exchange sends into the next column, so 4□2 - 185 = 217 is answered from the ones column alone.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Substitute the chosen digit back and work the whole question through, column by column.
misconceptions.source: SPEC.md section 3.4 (taxonomy section 11 error list); visible only in the working box

misconceptions.name: Adds the two numbers a missing-number question shows
misconceptions.description: Reads 7 + □ = 12 as 'add what you see': writes 19 instead of 5.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Say the sentence aloud as a story; find the part, not the whole
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/items.py (generator-declared; added to the vocabulary 2026-09-20 after engine audit found them on 1,172 live items with no row)

misconceptions.name: Reads '=' as 'write the answer here'
misconceptions.description: In 6 + 4 = □ + 3 writes 10, the total of the left side, ignoring the right.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Balance scale with rods: both sides must weigh the same
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/items.py (generator-declared; added to the vocabulary 2026-09-20 after engine audit found them on 1,172 live items with no row)

misconceptions.name: Adds every number on the page
misconceptions.description: In 6 + 4 = □ + 3 writes 13: the three numbers added together.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Cover one side; ask what would make the two sides match
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/items.py (generator-declared; added to the vocabulary 2026-09-20 after engine audit found them on 1,172 live items with no row)

misconceptions.name: Stops after the first step of a two-step question
misconceptions.description: Answers 'had 40, spent 15, then earned 8' with 25 — the first step only.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Underline both things that happen before calculating; two boxes for two steps
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/items.py (generator-declared; added to the vocabulary 2026-09-20 after engine audit found them on 1,172 live items with no row)

misconceptions.name: Adds the amounts spent and forgets the budget
misconceptions.description: Asked what is left of 8000 after 2400, 900 and 700, writes 4000 — the spending.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask what the question wants: the money gone, or the money left?
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/items.py (generator-declared; added to the vocabulary 2026-09-20 after engine audit found them on 1,172 live items with no row)

misconceptions.name: A hundred out
misconceptions.description: The answer is one hundred less than the correct total, from a miscounted hundreds column.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the answer aloud in place value; estimate to the nearest hundred first
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/items.py (generator-declared; added to the vocabulary 2026-09-20 after engine audit found them on 1,172 live items with no row)

misconceptions.name: Multiplies each digit and drops the carry
misconceptions.description: Writes only the last digit of each digit's product: 34 × 6 written as 84.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Column multiplication with the carry written above; say 'twenty-four is two tens and four ones'
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-20; written after `engine goal w1-build-the-bank` found 14 of 20 multiplication questions undiagnosable)

misconceptions.name: Writes each digit's whole product side by side
misconceptions.description: Writes the products of the tens and the ones next to each other: 34 × 6 written as 1824.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Grid (area) method first, then the column method beside it
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-20; written after `engine goal w1-build-the-bank` found 14 of 20 multiplication questions undiagnosable)

misconceptions.name: Adds the carry before multiplying instead of after
misconceptions.description: Adds the carried digit to the next digit and then multiplies: 34 × 6 written as 304.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Say the order aloud: multiply, then add what was carried
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-20; written after `engine goal w1-build-the-bank` found 14 of 20 multiplication questions undiagnosable)

misconceptions.name: Multiplies the ones digit and stops
misconceptions.description: Only the ones digit is multiplied: 34 × 6 written as 24.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Grid method: show that both parts of the number are multiplied
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-20; written after `engine goal w1-build-the-bank` found 14 of 20 multiplication questions undiagnosable)

misconceptions.name: One row out in the times table
misconceptions.description: Answers the row above in the table: 34 × 6 written as 170, which is 34 × 5.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Count on in that table; check against a known fact
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-20; written after `engine goal w1-build-the-bank` found 14 of 20 multiplication questions undiagnosable)

misconceptions.name: Added instead of multiplying
misconceptions.description: Writes the sum where the product was asked: 34 × 6 written as 40.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the question aloud; identify the operation word
misconceptions.source: packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-20; written after `engine goal w1-build-the-bank` found 14 of 20 multiplication questions undiagnosable)

misconceptions.name: Writes only the units digit of each product, ones column first
misconceptions.description: Multiplies each digit but writes only the units digit of each product, ones first: 34 × 2 written as 86, 56 × 3 as 85.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Grid method: write each whole product in its place, then add them
misconceptions.source: Aseem's Grade 3 reports to parents, 2026-09 — W3's gold (ADR 0028); packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (MUL_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-21)

misconceptions.name: Writes the comparison sign the wrong way round
misconceptions.description: Knows which number is greater but turns the sign the wrong way: 456 > 465.
misconceptions.repair_hint: The open side faces the bigger number; read it aloud as 'is less than'
misconceptions.source: Aseem's Grade 3 reports to parents, 2026-09 — W3's gold (ADR 0028); packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (COMPARE_PREDICTORS, 2026-09-21)

misconceptions.name: Loses a digit when copying out the answer
misconceptions.description: Works the answer out and loses one digit writing it down: 62,413 written as 6,243.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Check the final answer against the working, digit by digit, before moving on
misconceptions.source: Aseem's Grade 3 reports to parents, 2026-09 — W3's gold (ADR 0028); packages/engine/engine/assess/misconceptions.py (ANSWER_RULES, 2026-09-21)

misconceptions.name: Takes the exchange from the wrong column — the hundreds, not the tens
misconceptions.description: The ones need an exchange and the ten is taken from the hundreds; the tens are left as they were, so the answer is 90 short: 352 − 178 written as 84.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Rods: the ten always comes from the column next door
misconceptions.source: Addition & Subtraction Assessment Skill Taxonomy §11 (school team), step 8g

misconceptions.name: Turns the subtraction round: takes away the two numbers the question shows
misconceptions.description: On □ − 7 = 8 writes 1 (8 − 7), as if subtraction could be done in either order.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read □ − 7 = 8 as 'something take away 7 leaves 8'; check by adding back
misconceptions.source: Addition & Subtraction Assessment Skill Taxonomy §11 (school team), step 8g

misconceptions.name: Accepts an answer without checking its size
misconceptions.description: Says 487 + 216 could be 6,903: an answer with a digit too many (or too few) is not caught by estimating first.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Estimate before answering; ask 'about how big should this be?'
misconceptions.source: Addition & Subtraction Assessment Skill Taxonomy §11 (school team), step 8g

misconceptions.name: Gets odd and even the wrong way round
misconceptions.description: Says odd + odd is odd, or even − odd is even: the ones digits decide, and the rule is applied backwards.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Pairs of counters: an odd number always has one left over
misconceptions.source: Addition & Subtraction Assessment Skill Taxonomy §11 (school team), step 8g

misconceptions.name: Does not compare estimate to exact answer
misconceptions.description: The child calculates the estimate correctly and the exact answer correctly but does not check whether they are close, or states they are close when they are far apart.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: is the difference between your estimate and your exact answer smaller than 10?

misconceptions.name: Reverses the claim's truth value
misconceptions.description: The child judges a true claim as false, or a false claim as true, then explains reasoning that fits their wrong judgment.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask the child to test the claim with concrete materials (rods or counters) before deciding if it is true or false.

misconceptions.name: Rounds one number only
misconceptions.description: The child rounds only the first number to the nearest ten and uses the second number unchanged, or rounds only the second number.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Use a place-value chart to show which numbers need rounding before you estimate.
